incident.summary: Card payments are slow and failing at checkout
incident.context: Support reports checkout errors since about 10:00 UTC.

headline: Investigation into Card Payment Failures at Checkout
summary: The investigation into the card payment failures indicates a strong likelihood of issues stemming from a saturation of the database connection pool due to a configuration change. However, various hypotheses present competing claims regarding the exact cause of the problems struggling through external dependencies and the transaction loads on the payments-api. Further evidence is needed to fully clarify the causative factors.

observed_impact.text: At 10:02, an ERROR log from payments-api indicated a timeout waiting for a DB connection from pool after 3000ms.

evidence.text: 2026-09-01T10:02:00Z payments-api ERROR: Timed out waiting for DB connection from pool after 3000ms

observed_impact.text: At 10:05, another ERROR log reported a similar timeout waiting for a DB connection from pool after 3000ms.

evidence.text: 2026-09-01T10:05:00Z payments-api ERROR: Timed out waiting for DB connection from pool after 3000ms

observed_impact.text: At 10:06, a WARNING log showed that the connection pool was saturated with all connections in use and 52 waiting.

evidence.text: 2026-09-01T10:06:00Z payments-api WARNING: Connection pool saturated: 8/8 in use, 52 waiting

observed_impact.text: At 10:07, an ERROR log from api-gateway indicated a 504 response from payments-api during the checkout process.

evidence.text: 2026-09-01T10:07:00Z api-gateway ERROR: Upstream payments-api returned 504 for POST /checkout/pay

observed_impact.text: At 10:14, another ERROR log reported a timeout from payments-api similar to earlier messages.

evidence.text: 2026-09-01T10:14:00Z payments-api ERROR: Timed out waiting for DB connection from pool after 3000ms

observed_impact.text: At 10:27, an ERROR log from payments-api indicated yet another timeout while waiting for a DB connection.

evidence.text: 2026-09-01T10:27:00Z payments-api ERROR: Timed out waiting for DB connection from pool after 3000ms

observed_impact.text: The db_pool_utilization_percent metric peaked at 102% at 10:15.
Error rate percent for payments-api peaked at 7.65% at 10:15 and was 7.61% at 10:00, indicating an increase in errors during the incident.
Latency at the 95th percentile reached 2448 ms at 10:15, suggesting increased response times from the payments-api during the incident.

hypotheses.title: Connection Pool Saturation Due to Reduced Pool Size
hypotheses.assessment: Strong evidence supports that the connection pool size reduction to 8 from 40 has likely caused saturation, leading to timeouts. However, direct correlations with transaction loads and their role in escalating errors remain uncertain.

supporting.text: [fact] A configuration change was made to the payments-api at 09:55 UTC to reduce the database connection pool size from 40 to 8.

based_on.text: 2026-09-01T09:55:00Z CHG-E01-2 payments-api config_change (succeeded): Reduce database connection pool size {"key": "db.pool.max_size", "new": "8", "old": "40"}

hypotheses.title: External Dependency Latency Issues
hypotheses.assessment: While high latency from the fraud-check service is plausible, contradictory evidence indicates that observed 504 errors occurred alongside connection timeouts rather than being influenced by external services.

supporting.text: [fact] The payments-api is related to external dependencies including a fraud-check service with a 2000ms client timeout.

contradicting.text: [fact] At 10:07, an ERROR log from api-gateway indicated a 504 response from payments-api during the checkout process.

based_on.text: 2026-09-01T10:07:00Z api-gateway ERROR: Upstream payments-api returned 504 for POST /checkout/pay

hypotheses.title: Increased Load on Payments-API
hypotheses.assessment: Evidence suggests a peak in error rates and latency possibly correlates with increased load. However, critical missing metrics on transaction volume prevent a conclusive determination.

supporting.text: [fact] Error rate percent for payments-api peaked at 7.65% at 10:15 and was 7.61% at 10:00, indicating an increase in errors during the incident.
[fact] Latency at the 95th percentile reached 2448 ms at 10:15, suggesting increased response times from the payments-api during the incident.

hypotheses.title: Legacy Bug in Payments-API
hypotheses.assessment: No supporting evidence has been presented to validate the notion of a legacy bug causing this incident.

hypotheses.title: Database Performance Issues
hypotheses.assessment: Although the possibility of performance issues exists, there appears to be insufficient evidence linking database performance as a significant contributing factor to the failures.

supporting.text: [fact] The payments-api is critically dependent on the postgres-payments database.

facts.text: A database connection pool size reduction was executed at 09:55, prior to the incident.

evidence.text: [fact] A configuration change was made to the payments-api at 09:55 UTC to reduce the database connection pool size from 40 to 8.

facts.text: Payments-api logs indicate timeouts due to connection pool saturation, with multiple ERROR logs observed at approximately 10:02 and 10:05.

facts.text: Error rates for payments-api peaked at 7.65% during the incident timeline, indicating increased failure rates.
Latency at the 95th percentile reached 2448ms at 10:15, suggesting performance issues aligning with reported failures.
The db_pool_utilization_percent metric peaked at 102% at 10:15, indicating a saturated connection pool causing timeouts.

immediate_actions: Restore database connection pool size to previous limits (40) to mitigate current saturation issues. (for H1)
follow_up_actions: Monitor connection pool utilization and error rates continuously for the next week to ensure stability after changes. (for H1)
preventive_actions: Implement improved logging for fraud-check service to measure latency and error occurrences. (for H2)
Collect and analyze traffic patterns during future incidents to ensure adequate capacity and performance of payments-api. (for H3)
open_questions: What external factors contributed to the spike in transaction volume during the incident?
Could any additional configuration or environmental changes impact the payments-api performance trends observed?
limitations: Critic round limit reached with verdict 'revise'; issues may remain unresolved.
Metrics for request rates leading into the incident were not available, hindering traffic analysis.
Performance metrics for the postgres database during peak events were missing.
